subject: Observability readiness for go-live — dashboards & runbook transfer
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <ops@stellarmed.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observability readiness for go-live — dashboards & runbook transfer

Hi Ben —

We're aiming for a soft go-live for StellarMed on Aug 29 and want to make sure the observability handoff is complete before that date. Specifically we need:
- A production-ready dashboards bundle (errors, latency P50/P95, token-cost breakdown) we can drop into our Grafana.
- Tracing hook examples for our Java service (how to attach request_id, span naming conventions).
- An error taxonomy for operational vs user errors plus suggested alert severities.
- A runbook (play-by-play) for common incidents (high latency, KV cache miss storm, model fallback).
- Clear alert routing (who owns what during PST business hours and on-call escalation).

Nicole (cc) is our engineering PM and will coordinate the vetting; we're tracking a few pre-go-live load tests next week. Attached is a small sample of production traffic characteristics to help size dashboards.

Can you confirm the plan and whether Redwood will provide the runbook template and tracing snippets?

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Operations
StellarMed
(attachment: prod-traffic-sample.csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <ops@stellarmed.com>
Cc: Nicole Park <nicole.park@stellarmed.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability readiness for go-live — dashboards & runbook transfer

Alex — thanks for the clear checklist. We can support all items on your list and I'd like to propose a short preflight plan so we hit Aug 29 confidently. High-level: 

1) Deliverables this week (by Fri 2027-08-20):
   - Redwood runbook template (play-by-play runbook PDF) — attached.
   - Grafana dashboard json export (errors, latency, throughput, token-cost) — will share Drive link when ready.
   - Trace hook checklist (Java snippet + naming guidance) — attached CSV + snippet.

2) Owners and routing:
   - Level 1 alerts (operational): StellarMed SREs.
   - Level 2 (service degradation, model fallback): Redwood on-call (primary) with Jordan as escalation contact during PST business hours.
   - Post-mortem owner: StellarMed PM (Nicole) + Redwood CS for joint RCA.

3) Action: Let's set a 45-min alignment call Monday 2027-08-16 @ 10:00 PT to review dashboards and run the trace snippet on a staging request. I've invited Laura and Jordan to cover runbooks and alerting.

I attached the runbook template and a trace-hook checklist that includes the snippet we use for injecting request_id/span_id and a small list of recommended span names. Laura — can you confirm the alert routing mapping and whether we should add any Redwood service-level synthetic checks?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachments: redwood-runbook-template_v2.pdf, trace-hook-checklist.csv)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

On Sun, Aug 15, 2027 at 10:03 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the clear checklist. We can support all items on your list and I'd like to propose a short preflight plan so we hit Aug 29 confidently. High-level: 
>
> 1) Deliverables this week (by Fri 2027-08-20):
>    - Redwood runbook template (play-by-play runbook PDF) — attached.
>
Thanks Ben — adding a few engineering-specific details that will make the runbook and dashboards actionable for StellarMed's SREs. Below are the concrete checklist items I'll own and bring to Monday's call: 

Runbook (what I'll provide)
- Incident play names and short-check actions: high-latency, increased 5xx rate, KV cache pressure, model-fallback loop.
- Quick triage steps (verify model variant, check recent rollouts, check KV cache metric + eviction rate).
- Pager tree + escalation matrix (Redwood on-call hours, contact points, 15-min SLA for fallback).

Dashboards / Tracing
- Grafana panels: per-route latency P50/P95/P99, tokens-per-request histogram, model-variant breakdown, 5xx spike heatmap.
- Traces: include sample Java snippet in trace-snippet.txt that sets trace id and attaches model.variant and request.size tags. (I'll attach the snippet.)
- Synthetic checks: add a low-volume synthetic that runs the most common route every 5m — flagged to Redwood on-call if p95 increases by >40% vs baseline.

Alert taxonomy mapping (short):
- Severity: P0 (service down), P1 (degraded >25% of requests), P2 (cost/regression risk), P3 (info/actionable next day).
- Suggested owners: P0/P1 Redwood on-call + StellarMed SRE; P2 Redwood CS + StellarMed eng; P3 StellarMed eng.

Preflight tests for Monday's call
- Import dashboard JSON into a staging Grafana instance and validate panel queries against sample traffic.
- Run trace snippet on staging; verify spans appear with request_id and correct tags.
- Trigger synthetic check and validate routing to Redwood on-call.

I'll attach the trace snippet now. Jordan — can you confirm the exact Redwood on-call alias for PST business hours so I can put it in the runbook?

Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachments: trace-snippet.txt)
